Findings.problem: The step mutators discard their documented transitions at the public contract boundary. In particular, push cannot be followed by size/pop on the same id, and a Some loose id returned by pop/take cannot be used for push: neither domain membership nor the inserted/removed identity follows from inv alone.
Findings.key_premise: The mutation contracts expose invariant preservation but omit map transitions; related gaps occur in step_push_back, step_insert_before_at, step_cursor_insert_before, successful pop/take variants, and frame clauses on cursor/new/drop steps.
Findings.suggestion: Specify the affected map domains and entries, loose-handle consumption/production, list sequence edits and preservation of unrelated entries; for Some(lid), ensure fresh lid membership and the popped slot identity. Export unchanged maps on cursor moves/checkouts and freed slots on list drop. Keep nondeterministic newly minted list IDs abstract.

Findings.problem: step_cursor_mut_at claims to mirror rejection of non-safe addresses, but checks only the page index. An unaligned address one byte into a listed frame has the same frame_to_index and yields true, whereas get_slot rejects it.
Findings.key_premise: frame_to_index is paddr / PAGE_SIZE; get_slot explicitly returns NotAligned on paddr % PAGE_SIZE != 0, and this step has no alignment precondition.
Findings.suggestion: Guard both the membership result and implementation branch with has_safe_slot(frame), as step_contains already does; preserve the unchanged-store guarantee for that miss.

Findings.problem: push_back_embedded is documented as splicing at the tail but promises insertion before the last element. For [A,B] and C it produces [A,C,B], contradicting the promised back insertion and the next pop_back expectation.
Findings.key_premise: Both the helper body and the corresponding executable push_back use the last-element cursor with insert_before.
Findings.suggestion: Align the executable back insertion and embedding with insertion at old length (the ghost/end position), then state the append sequence result; retain the corresponding neighbor-frame conditions.

Compliance.compliance_or_na_reason: Store validity and held-resource membership express ownership protocol. Empty/out-of-range take operations accept requests and return None rather than demanding success; embedded nonempty take requirements apply only to successful primitives.
